nodes.label: Multi-channel messaging: SMS/WhatsApp/email carried on the in-app chat tables
Rationale: chat_channels.last_channel records the last medium used so replies default to that channel
Unknown-number SMS inbox for inbound texts that match no customer
Linking an unknown SMS thread to a customer record after the fact
Twilio delivery-status webhook audit trail
Managed Twilio 10DLC brand and campaign registration state held on tenants
Rationale: SMS RLS resolves the tenant through an app_users subquery instead of get_user_tenant_id()
Configurable monthly pricing-tier threshold (30 or 31 days) per tenant
Rationale: the same threshold doubles as the pro-rata divisor for monthly rate maths
Per-tenant custom booking and portal domains replacing {slug}.drive-247.com
Gotcha: the DB row alone routes nothing — the domain must also be added in Vercel with DNS pointed there
Rationale: partial indexes exist because middleware resolves the custom domain on every single request
Deposit pre-authorisation hold tracked directly on the rental row
Hold status vocabulary: held / captured / released / expired / refreshing
Rationale: holds are placed at key giving, released at key receiving and auto-refreshed for long rentals
Payment method and Stripe customer stamped on the rental so the hold can be re-authorised off-session
Tesla Fleet API integration for Supercharger re-billing
Tenant-level Tesla OAuth token, refresh token and expiry with a test/live mode switch
Per-vehicle Fleet API enablement and Tesla vehicle identifier
Supercharger sessions recorded per rental and re-billed (pending / charged / waived / partially_charged)
'Supercharger' added to the ledger_entries category whitelist so charges can be posted
Gotcha: the ledger category CHECK is one big whitelist — adding a category means restating all twenty
Scheduled auto-send of lockbox codes at a configurable offset before rental start
Rationale: a NULL offset means manual-only send and 0 means exactly at start time
rentals.lockbox_sent_at is the idempotency stamp that stops a minute-frequency cron re-sending
Lockbox send audit log (scheduled / sent / resent / rescheduled / failed) per delivery channel
Partial index selecting only unsent lockbox rentals, which is the cron's scan path
Gotcha: the 'Service role can manage' policy carries no TO clause, so USING(true) grants every role full write access
Rescheduling a rental clears lockbox_sent_at so the cron re-evaluates the send time
The reset also writes a 'rescheduled' audit row carrying the old and new pickup window
Automated vehicle-return reminders, enabled per tenant with an hours-before-end window
rentals.return_reminder_sent_at is the send-once stamp for the reminder cron
Turnaround buffer keeping a vehicle unavailable for N minutes after a rental ends
Rationale: default 0 preserves the pre-existing no-buffer behaviour for every tenant
Buffer ceiling raised from 8 hours to 72 hours by restating the CHECK constraint
rentals.approved_at records the moment a rental was approved
Rationale: approval time (not booking time) is the anchor for lockbox auto-send timing
Browser voice calling through Twilio using a per-tenant TwiML app and API key pair
call_logs: per-call lifecycle record keyed by the Twilio CallSid
Rationale: call_logs INSERT/UPDATE policies are WITH CHECK(false) so only service_role edge functions can write
'voice' folded into the chat channel vocabulary, unifying calls with messaging threads
Gotcha: the Twilio API key secret and auth token sit in plain tenants columns with no encryption
Tenant-isolated blog: categories, posts and version history
Draft/published workflow with full SEO metadata, canonical URL, noindex and reading time
Anonymous role reads published posts and all categories so the booking site can render the blog
Gotcha: authenticated blog policies are USING(true) — tenant isolation is deferred to the app layer, copying the cms_pages pattern
A 'blog' CMS page added to the new-tenant seed function and backfilled for existing tenants
blog_post_versions snapshots title, content and metadata each time a post is published
NOTIFY pgrst so PostgREST reloads its schema cache and the new tables are queryable immediately
pg_cron job calling the send-lockbox-scheduled edge function every minute
Rationale: minute-frequency is safe only because the function picks rows where lockbox_sent_at IS NULL
Gotcha: the Supabase project URL is hardcoded in the cron body instead of read from a runtime setting
Gotcha: the cron posts no Authorization header, so the endpoint is callable by anyone who knows the URL
Ambiguity: the tenant setting is documented as minutes before rental start, yet the cron comment describes approved_at + offset
pg_cron job calling the send-return-reminders edge function every 15 minutes
Double-booking prevention: at most one non-terminal rental per vehicle per date range
Rationale: a trigger rather than a GiST exclusion constraint, so pre-existing overlapping rows do not fail the migration
Cancelled, Rejected and Closed rentals, and rentals with no vehicle assigned, are exempt from the check
Open-ended rentals coalesce to 9999-12-31, so a missing end date blocks the vehicle indefinitely
Gotcha: the overlap trigger compares raw dates and ignores tenants.buffer_time_minutes, so the turnaround buffer is app-layer only
Pay-As-You-Go rental billing foundation: tenant policy, per-rental state and accrual bookkeeping
Tenant PAYG policy defaults: reminder interval, grace period, reminder cap, pre-auth days, max duration
Per-rental reminder interval override; NULL falls back to the tenant default
Per-rental accrual cursor: start anchor, last/next accrual timestamps, day count, pause and close stamps
UNIQUE(rental_id, accrual_day_index) makes cron double-posting structurally impossible
is_partial and hours_covered carry the pro-rated final day when an admin closes a rental mid-cycle
payg_accruals.ledger_entry_ids back-references the ledger rows each accrual created
Rationale: PAYG reuses the existing Rental / Tax / Service Fee ledger categories, so no CHECK constraint change was needed
Safety cap: accrual halts and an admin alert fires after payg_max_duration_days, deduped by payg_max_duration_alerted
payg_reminder_log: one row per reminder attempt with outstanding amount, days active and days overdue
Partial indexes scoped to open PAYG rentals are the scan path for both the accrual and reminder crons
Rationale: SELECT-only tenant RLS with no write policy at all, because edge functions use service_role and bypass RLS
Gotcha: the cron indexes filter on rentals.is_pay_as_you_go, a column this migration never creates
Pivot from managed Twilio subaccounts to tenant bring-your-own Twilio accounts
Rationale: a bare column rename with no data migration, because no production tenant was on a subaccount yet
10DLC brand and campaign tracking dropped — under BYO tenants register 10DLC in their own Twilio console
twilio_messaging_service_sid kept as an optional override for higher-volume tenants
twilio_connection_verified_at stamps a successful tenant credential check
pg_cron job calling accrue-payg-charges every 15 minutes
Project URL resolved at runtime from app.settings.supabase_url rather than a hardcoded host
pg_cron job calling send-payg-reminders hourly
Rationale: an hourly tick with the due decision made per rental inside the function supports any tenant timezone
Every customer gets a chat channel at insert time so operators can message them immediately
Rationale: channels were previously created lazily by the booking customer portal, so operators never saw customers who did not open chat
One-shot backfill creating a channel for every pre-existing customer
Call forwarding to staff phones with voicemail fallback
app_users.forwarding_number holds each operator's personal phone for forwarded calls
Voicemail recordings with listened/listened-by tracking, linked to the call log and chat channel
Private 'voicemails' storage bucket holding the recorded audio
Gotcha: the voicemail storage policies key only on bucket_id with no tenant scoping, so they isolate nothing between tenants
Call recording plus AI transcript, summary and action items stored on the call log
Per-tenant call_recording_enabled toggle gates whether calls are recorded at all
Post-audit remediation of the PAYG cron chain: missing RPC, unauthenticated crons, duplicate ledger charges
increment_payg_reminder_count RPC bumps the counter and stamps the send time in one statement
Rationale: the edge function already called this RPC; with it missing every call silently degraded to a racy read-then-write
PAYG cron jobs re-scheduled to send a service_role Authorization header
Rationale: without an Authorization header the cron endpoints were callable by anyone who knew the Supabase project URL
Unique partial index on ledger_entries.reference for payg-% Charge rows blocks duplicate charges when an accrual rollback fails
Active-template and template-name uniqueness re-scoped per (tenant, template_category)
Rationale: the old index allowed only one active template per tenant across all categories, so a PAYG template could not coexist with the standard one

hyperedges.label: Pay-As-You-Go billing cycle: schema, accrual cron, reminder cron, audit hardening
Lockbox scheduled-send flow: tenant offset, approval anchor, reschedule reset, minute cron, audit log
Twilio omnichannel customer comms: SMS threads, voice calls, forwarding/voicemail, recording, BYO account
